text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Headphones, Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds by Anker, Bluetooth 5.0, 8H Battery, IPX7 Waterproof, SweatGuard, Comfortable Wireless Headphones, Secure Fit for Running, Gym, Workout These are around the same price as all the junky Chinese wireless earbud brands on Amazon but sound much better, are much more reliable, and are made by a company with good customer service that stands behind their products.

Ankers has several wireless earbuds with the cords that go behind the neck but only these, the spirit, the spirit pro, and the spirit x are worth considering for purchase. Their other earbuds are older models that cost just as much but have less features and weaker specs.

The bass on these is weak but I use these mostly for working out and for that it is fine.

I already have a pair of Apple EarPods but I wanted another wireless pair of headphones as well so I could switch back and forth while the other pair was charging.

These do not work with Apples w1 chip Bluetooth protocol, only apple and beats headphones work with that standard right now so those wireless headphones brands will sound better than anything other wireless headphones will with Apple products.

They also do not have aptx, which is the best sounding Bluetooth standard for anything other than Apple.

Ankers spirit pro headphones do support the aptx standard and supposedly have better bass than these so those are that models advantages.

However the spirit pro cost twice as much as these and only supports Bluetooth protocol 4.1 while these headphones support Bluetooth protocol 5.0.

Why is that important? Because the 5.0 protocol is the new “low energy” Bluetooth standard. Meaning that if you have both a device and headphones that support it you will get much more play time out of the same size battery.

Ankers other most recent model of earbuds, the spirit x headphones, have the same specs as these headphones in terms of the protocols they support but have a different form factor, obviously, and have 10mm drivers while these have 6mm. They also have a little more battery life.

I think I might buy the spirit x headphones as well in order to have a backup and to compare their sound.

As an Apple user the spirit pro headphones are just not worth the extra cost for me since I will never use the aptx protocol and they do not even support the Bluetooth 5.0 protocol.
If they were Bluetooth 5.0 compatible I might consider spending the extra 25 bucks in order to get that extra bass.

While these don’t sound spectacular they will get great battery life when I use them with devices that support 5.0 Bluetooth and they are very affordable.

I want to quickly rant about amazons policies and the flood of cheap Chinese products on here.

If you search for “wireless earbuds” or “Bluetooth earbuds” or any similar terms ankers products will not even show up on the first several pages of results.
Nor will Aukeys headphones, which I think are the second best option for wireless headphones in this price range.

Why is this?
Because the Chinese brands pay “click farms” to leave hundreds or even thousands of 5 star reviews.

The fraud is so obvious. What do you think is happening when a product has more than a thousand 5 star reviews all left on the same day or within the same few days and almost none of those reviews are from verified buyers?
The fact that many of them say the same things over and over and that many of them are written in broken English are other obvious clues.

I reported a few of them but Amazon does not take them down because Amazon cares about money and absolutely nothing else and having millions of people purchase this Chinese junk off their website makes them a lot of money.

It really sucks because good products, like these anker headphones, are barely visible in amazon search results because reputable brands don’t pay click farms to manipulate amazon search results.

It’s the consumers that lose in the end when their headphones, or other cheap Chinese products, break a few weeks after use or maybe never even work to begin with.
And you can bet that half of the time the companies selling this junk on amazon will simply disappear in order to avoid accepting returns and then reappear later under a new seller account to sell more junk through click farm manipulated amazon search results.

Of course amazon will find itself on the hook for some of these costs but apparently the money they make off of allowing all of this Chinese junk to be sold on their website under false practices is much more than any costs they incur.

These practices that amazon allows, and this one issue about manipulated search results is just the tip of the iceberg, hurts not just American consumers it also hurts American companies.

Rant over.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones, Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds by Anker, Bluetooth 5.0, 8H Battery, IPX7 Waterproof, SweatGuard, Comfortable Wireless Headphones, Secure Fit for Running, Gym, Workout

TP-Link USB WiFi Adapter for PC(TL-WN725N), N150 Wireless Network Adapter for Desktop - Nano Size WiFi Dongle for Windows 11/10/7/8/8.1/XP/ Mac OS 10.9-10.15 Linux Kernel 2.6.18-4.4.3, 2.4GHz Only At first I struggled to get this adapter to work with Linux. I plugged it into the computer --- nothing. Then I went to the website and found the driver package, which had to be downloaded, then followed the instructions to install it from the command line (along with some other items had to be installed as well). I tried installing the beta and stable driver packages, and the installation failed both times.

I had about given up. Even though I bought the adapter on sale, I considered returning it. I did another search for TP-Link drivers for Linux, and found a suggestion in the replies to an article on installing WiFi drivers:

Turn off the computer, plug in the dongle, then reboot the computer.

. . .

That did it. The system loaded drivers and the adapter worked fine, and worked much better than the old adapter I was replacing. I did have to type in the password to reconnect to the WiFi network, but that was it. Works great now.

That worked with an Ubuntu-based version of Linux. Getting it to work with Debian Linux was a little different. I did a search for "wifi" in Synaptic package manager, and found and installed a package called "firmware-realtek." (You may have to add or check "non-free" repositories for it to show up.) I rebooted and now it works great with Debian Linux.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link USB WiFi Adapter for PC(TL-WN725N), N150 Wireless Network Adapter for Desktop - Nano Size WiFi Dongle for Windows 11/10/7/8/8.1/XP/ Mac OS 10.9-10.15 Linux Kernel 2.6.18-4.4.3, 2.4GHz Only

text_fidelity_a:
Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 1 camera kit UPDATE (8/4/2019):
After some recent system updates, I have found that the 5 sec video may not be accessible until after someone has left the area. It was not that snappy before, but now it seems to be slower in accessing the video from my phone.
Additionally, I have had packages put on my front deck / steps that is 10 feet away from my front door and the Blink XT2 camera, but the video was never triggered. The Blink is aimed in that direction. So I have changed the sensitivity from 5 to 9, the highest. Also, I have changed the clip length to 10 seconds. We shall see how this functions.

Since I have had the Blink XT2 less than a week, I will update when I know more about how long the batteries last.

READ THE INSTRUCTIONS BEFORE BEGINNING INSTALLATION.

Download the app first. Once the app is downloaded, it will prompt you as to what has to be done. Use the device to take a photo of (read) the camera’s ID (QR code) OR enter the Serial Number manually.

Open the camera - Remove the back cover by holding down the gray ‘button’ while pulling the bottom of the back cover away from the camera body. It has a rubber or silicone gasket in the groove around the cover. Because it has a friction fit, it can be difficult to pry off the cover. I could put a little lube on the sealing gasket, but it might cause problems if it reacts with either the plastic or the gasket.

All synching has to be done while the camera is open, then it is put together before mounting it. The Sync module has to remain plugged into an AC outlet, so find a convenient place for the module to rest or hang.

The back cover is replaced by pressing it firmly where the posts are located until a ‘click’ is heard near each corner.

I used the base of the mount to locate and drill 2 small holes in the wood. Then I put the screws into the mount and the base and attached the mount to the house. After the base is attached, the cam is pressed onto the mount. That was the hard part.

The mount attaches to the hole in the back cover by pressing the assembled camera onto the mount. This should be done after the mount is attached to the desired location using the two screws included.

I had installed the camera as high as I could above my front door. Most of the videos showed the top of my head, nothing as to identifying me from my face. So I thought I would move it a little lower, still above the door; and as I turned the camera so I could use a long screwdriver to remove the screws, it came off the mount and fell onto the floor. Apparently, it suffered no ill effects. Perhaps the very warm temperatures made the plastic loose enough for it to come off easily. I would like to have a more secure mounting system. I have ordered a mount that has a cover to hold Blink XT2 securely.

At bottom of the Home screen of the app, be sure to slide the switch so that it says Armed.
Had to go into settings (not labeled as that) and ENABLE motion sensor. On the Home screen of the app, the serial number of the camera is printed less than halfway down and on the left. On the right side, a symbol of three lines appears. Press this and it opens Camera Settings. This is where Enable is located for MOTION DETECTION.

The video length can be set but the default is 5 seconds. It can be turned on for Live View which is almost continuous recording. 

In the next week, I will attempt to “see” what is happening at my front door. I am hoping there will be no problem getting notifications when someone comes to my front door.

UPDATED AFTER USING A FEW DAYS:
In a location that has no Wi-Fi access and spotty cell coverage, I was able to view the delivery person bringing my package to my door.

The mount I ordered is a two-piece plastic enclosure that is attached to an aluminum base that is attached to the wall using 3 screws. First I drilled 3 pilot holes (5/64" drill bit) for the screws. They were tightened using a manual screwdriver so the aluminum would not crack. I plugged the hole on the bottom of the case where the USB cable could be used to charge rechargeable batteries. The foam that is used to package the Blink is too dense and stiff, so I used some closed-cell foam that came with another product.
text_fidelity_b: Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 1 camera kit

I ordered two watch/chest-strap Garmin 110s, one for me, one for the wife. Hers worked fine, but after about 45 days got condensation on the display while she was wearing it running or hiking. Condensation didn't just happen once. It happened several times, always while she was wearing it.

Mine works great, no condensation. Neither of us ever swim with the watch on, or have ever gotten it wet, besides normal sweat while running.

I contacted Garmin and told them all this, asked for an RMA. They responded with stupid question indicating they hadn't read my original email; did you get it wet? Did it happen when the watch went from a warm to a cold environment? Did you soak it in rice? NO! LIKE I SAID, the condensation happened while she was wearing it out running. So I emailed this back to Garmin. No response. I'm saying the waterproof to 1 meter thing is a crock.

On the other hand, mine works great. I like downloading it to endomondo, but the garmin.connect site is good too.

So it's a fifty-fifty proposition. You might get a good one. Or maybe not.

Also would be nice if there was a screen to display altitude.

VIDBOX Video Conversion Suite Time takes a toll on al things. but memories captured on old vhs, beta and 8mmm film need not be lost forever. This product presents an easy and fairly fool proof way to convert them to a more contemporary format. Set upt is easy. Use the included CD to install the software and driver. Then attach the the color coded cables to the vidbox, then the computer and then finally connect to your VCR, camcorder or other device. You then select your connector, settings and record You can review, burn to a dvd or publish if you desire. The menus are easy to follow and the process is simple overall. while this product converts and stores it does not improve the quality. The end product is a duplicate of the original.

My mother has boxes of old tapes and the like and we are converting them. She is in her mid eighties and is finding the process an enjoyable way to revisit happy occasions. It is turning out to be a fun project. So in the final analysis, a good product that does what it says.

text_fidelity_a: ADATA SU760 512GB 3D NAND 2.5 Inch SATA III Internal SSD (ASU760SS-512GT-C) Laptop is SO MUCH faster. Write and read date are fast too. Ultra quiet computer now that I swap the HDD with the SSD. I notice the fan doesn't kick on as often as it used to and when it does is not as loud either. Programs load and respond faster as well. text_fidelity_a:
ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK) I've bought and currently use both variants of the Relacon mouse. I'm putting this review on the wireless version.

Overall, 5 stars for the wireless with dongle, 3 stars for the Bluetooth. Unfortunately the Bluetooth one is a bit choppy with tracking, causing the pointer to jump to a random place on the screen often enough to be annoying. The dongle one doesn't have this issue for me. Otherwise they're identical in function and feel.

As a dedicated thumb trackball user since the early 90s, I love it! It is much better quality than any other ambidextrous thumb trackball I've optimistically tried over the years when looking for an alternative to the standard right (or rare left) dedicated handed thumb trackball. I have never been able to get comfortable or quick with finger trackballs, no matter how much I have wanted to or worked at it. Same with the Thinkpad trackpoint.

It is a physical relief to have a mouse that I can use in a neutral wrist position without having my hand or arm stretched out. It is especially nice to be able to transfer and use the mouse with my left hand when I need to type or do something else with my right.

I haven't installed the software or tried to remap the buttons. I just plug in the dongle or pair with Bluetooth, and Windows recognizes it. Since my displays are 1080 or smaller, I keep the speed or acceleration or dpi setting at 1 blink. The button is below the power switch, so I do accidentally tap it occasionally, but it's quick and easy to cycle back to 1.

The stand is more stylish than functional, and even with practice the mouse will sometimes slide right off, but at least it's included. Most of the time, I just switch it off and set the mouse on its side.
text_fidelity_b: ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK)

PixelFlash No-Bend Pins USB 3 CF Card Reader, Compact Flash Card Reader, Tactical SuperSpeed CompactFlash Memory Adapter, Rugged Anti-Scratch Exterior Classic Card Reader - White I was delighted to try out this CompactFlash reader, because my Canon camera uses CF cards, and my laptop has no card reader. My new computer will be lacking a CompactFlash card reader as well.

The claim of having pins that don't bend sounds extremely attractive to me, since I've tossed out a card reader in the past for getting bent pins that were hard to straighten.

While I didn't get to test out the USB 3.0 function of this card reader, it worked great on my regular USB 2.0 connections and speedily transferred over 500 photos in just a couple of minutes.

The only criticism I have of this card reader is that the profile is thick enough that on my computer, where I have two USB ports stacked one on top of another, I need to unplug something in order to be able to plug in this card reader. This isn't a big deal, since I have little USB extension cords that I can use if I truly don't want to unplug something else, but if the manufacturers are listening, I'd love to see a slimmer profile on any future models.

Overall, this is a fast, reasonably priced, handy little card reader that I'm glad to add to my collection of tech toys.

text_fidelity_a:
Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System It took me longer to unpack these than to get music via my iPod Touch streaming through them--the set-up, connecting, streaming process took under about two minutes. Worked fine as well with my laptop.

The sound quality is fine, especially for small speakers. I don't expect them to rattle my windows are pump the base. The lack of a strong bass is noticeable (as mentioned, not a surprise) but I wouldn't call them tinny at all. The sound was quite pleasing and handled high volume with no distortion.

They're small enough to pack or easily move around or outside. They do connect to each other, with detracts from their convenience a bit, and I personally wouldn't have minded a longer connecting cable so as to spread the sound a bit farther apart, but since they're really not made for room-filling sound--aimed more at desktop or otherwise small spaces, it's hard to call that a major complaint or oversight. A longer cable might have pleased me but had others complaining.

I prefer the Creative ZiiSound D3X to these--it's bit more convenient in that it's a single speaker set up and I thought its sound quality a little better, plus it has the ability to add in the subwoofer and other speakers (I have the subwoofer), but really, the difference isn't huge and the intent is somewhat different for most, so these speakers more than suit the bill for their size and purpose.
text_fidelity_b: Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 6 camera kit - Eco Packaging (VMS3630B) This is a truly wireless security camera system. The cameras operate on four CR123 batteries each, and lithium-ion batteries are included. That's a big plus, because you can install the cameras most anywhere. Setup took me a little over an hour.

It might be costly to replace lithium-ion batteries regularly, so you might consider getting rechargeable batteries.

The cameras are not pan-tilt-zoom cams. They're fixed. But the mounts are little metal domes, so you can manually aim the camera most any way you choose. The cameras have strong magnets in them to stick them firmly to the mounts. You can also stick the cameras to any steel or iron surface. You might keep in mind that since they're only held by magnets, the cams could be stolen easily if located in easy reach.

You start setup by downloading and installing the Arlo app on your device (phone, tablet, etc.) Then you create an account, agree to the terms, and follow the on-screen instructions for setup. The free version of the app supports up to six cameras.

The Netgear Arlo camera receiver/router connects to your Internet router with an Ethernet cable. It has a wall power supply with a six-foot cord. After it establishes a connection with the Internet router, you then pair the cameras, one by one, with the camera router. That takes about twenty seconds each.

This is where annoying things started. The app has motion detection on by default. Six cameras started slamming my email inbox and notification banner with motion detection alerts. It took a while to find the switch to turn motion detection off. You get to it by clicking on "mode" at the top, then the name you gave your camera system, then click on "disarm."

There's no batch delete feature in the app (not one I could find anyway) to delete all those motion detection videos at once. I had to go through and delete them one by one.

Notifications said the base unit and all the cams needed firmware updates. The update for the base unit went smoothly. The camera updates did not go so smoothly. Almost all of them said "update failed - camera rejected upgrade request." I moved the cameras close to the base unit and retried the updates, one camera at a time. Success.

These cameras do not continually take pictures, which is probably a battery saving feature. They start taking video or pictures only when motion detection is triggered, or when you manually click on "live" on each camera's thumbnail picture. The live stream takes several seconds to start. So the best setting for security would be motion detection active, but that might mean a lot of notifications. If you want to just take a look at the cameras to see what's up currently, that's kind of a problem. Each camera has to be started, and there's several seconds of wait time. (Edited to add: Adding to the wait time is that it appears video clips are not stored locally but rather uploaded to the manufacturer's site then downloaded back to your device.)

Let me put it this way: If motion detection is switched off and you hear the sound of a varmint on your porch and you want to take a quick look or grab a quick snapshot with one of these cameras, that's just not going to happen. You have to rely on motion detection being on to take the pictures for you. With motion detection off, at best you'll be able to take a look after several seconds of camera startup and buffering. (Edited to add: And if the varmint is moving quickly, you may not get a picture of it at all---just the motion detection alert and a short video that didn't capture what set the alert off.)

In contrast, I have three IP cameras that are always on. I can open the app for them and see a live picture from all three cams at once and grab a snapshot from any of them. But they all require hard-wired power, so it's a trade-off.

When you start the app, you see thumbnails from the last time you ran the live streams, or from the last motion detection. Those thumbnails can be hours old. I don't know if it would be possible, but if the Arlo app and cams had a "refresh all thumbnails" feature, that would be a big help in getting a current look at all your cameras. Then you could start live streams if you choose to.

For some reason the app will only support running five live streams out of the six cameras. You have to stop one of the streams to start the sixth.

If you install the Arlo app on more than one device, only one can be logged in and viewing cams at a time.

(Edited to add: A couple of other issues with the app: If you haven't opened the app in a while, you may get a notice that your login token has expired and you have to re-enter your password. More seconds lost if you got a motion detect alert and want to take a quick look. And sometimes you have to dismiss an ad before you can go look at the cams. And on my Kindle Fire, the Arlo app tends to go into some sort of loop sometimes, and I have to shut down and reboot the device.)

Picture quality is good. It can be set to lower resolution to maximize battery life, or medium or high resolution. The cams also have a night vision mode that can be switched off individually using the app. This is handy if you want to position the camera to look out a window at night. If the night vision mode is on, the IR led will reflect off the window at night like a bright light. Turning off night vision mode will avoid that. However, this still requires the exterior to be well lit or to have an outdoor IR source. The cameras' built in IR illumination isn't long range. It will light an average size room though.

The manufacturer says the cameras are weatherproof and can be positioned outdoors.

The web site says the cameras have a 300-foot range line-of-sight. One camera I placed about fifty feet from the router had difficulty connecting. It seems that the number of walls and other items between the camera and the router can have a big effect on connection, which isn't unusual with any wireless devices.

I think for a basic security system, IP cameras might have a few advantages over this system. But this system has its points, such as install-anywhere convenience and fairly simple setup. For actual security, keeping the system motion-detection armed and just letting the cameras grab and upload pictures and the app send notifications is the best solution, I would think. If you want to monitor live pictures yourself, or even just glance at very current pictures from time to time, I'd think this system wouldn't be a workable solution.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 6 camera kit - Eco Packaging (VMS3630B)

Acer Aspire 3 A314-23P-R3QA Slim Laptop | 14.0" Full HD IPS Display | AMD Ryzen 5 7520U Quad-Core Processor | AMD Radeon Graphics | 8GB LPDDR5 | 512GB NVMe SSD | Wi-Fi 6 | Windows 11 Home,Silver Pros

1. Very lightweight. It weighs only 4 pounds.
2. Excellent display. It has a full HD screen resolution of 1920x1080. In particular, high resolution digital photos look great on it.
3. Screen size is excellent. It measures a generous 15.6 inches
4. Hard drive is solid state. This makes booting the laptop extremely fast. It is up and running in a mere 30-45 seconds. My previous laptop, which had a mechanical drive, took as much as 10 minutes before it was fully ready to go.
5. Battery charge is good. It lasts up to 7.5 hours.
6. Attractive, modern design. The laptop is slim and sleek, with a lovely, silver color. I especially like the visibility of the backlit keyboard.
7. Excellent price. It offers good value for the cost.

Cons

1. Processing speed is only adequate. Though the speed is probably sufficient for the average user, it could be an issue if you are doing things that require a lot of horsepower, such as editing videos or creating music in digital-audio workstation software.
2. The 4GB of RAM is minimal. This amount of RAM is the very least that any user requires these days. However, it is upgradeable.
3. The hard drive is only 128GB in size. This is a surprisingly small amount for a modern computer. However, it is probably not a problem for the average user.
4. Windows Home "S Mode" may be an issue. It is automatically enabled on the laptop as a security protection for unwary, non-techie users, who might accidentally stray into dangerous territory online that could compromise the laptop. But for the more technically advanced and self-protectively-savvy user, this feature can be very annoying. Fortunately, those same techies can easily figure out how to disable it, which allows the laptop to run the regular Windows Home version.

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC P402BT Bluetooth Stereo Headphones with Integrated Mic, A2DP/AVRCP, 30-Hour Playback for Tablet/Smartphone/MP3 - Black These are pretty good bluetooth headphones. They excel with regard to comfort - the ear padding is plush and they have a nice balance between grip (e.g., staying put when you move) and comfort. The headband consists of 2 plastic rods without any padding, but doesn't cause a significant comfort issue.

I had zero problems pairing these with a couple of different tablets (Android operating system and the Fire version of Android). Simple, quick and painless. The operating range is also excellent, with zero dropouts at about 20 feet and only minor dropouts at 25+ feet.

The sound quality is quite good. While these open-ear designs don't have the booming bass quality of closed designs, I found the sound quality to be very good, especially in the midrange. They are an excellent choice for movie watching since the dialogue comes through so clearly.

I like the operating controls, especially the volume switch. It's a rocker-type design, so it's very easy to use without having to look at the button - just find it by feel, and press up to increase volume and down to decrease. The multifunction button is in the middle of the rocker switch and is very easy to find by touch as well.

The overall look is very snazzy, and the build quality appears solid.

There is only a modest amount of sound isolation, but that again is an issue inherent with open-ear headphones. It does cut ambient sound reasonably well - I had no problems listening to music while on a noisy treadmill without the ambient sound interfering to any significant degree.

Misses are the volume level. These have a rather limited upper volume range. Normally I set my tablet to about the 75% level and the headphone level to close to the upper point to get a good volume that blocks out ambient noise. With these, however, I had to set the tablet sound level to 100% and the earphone level also at 100%, and I still found them a bit lacking in volume. Given the price point, the range should be better.

But other than the volume issue, no complaints. Good sound, good comfort, great range and easy-to-use controls. Well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC P402BT Bluetooth Stereo Headphones with Integrated Mic, A2DP/AVRCP, 30-Hour Playback for Tablet/Smartphone/MP3 - Black

text_fidelity_a:
CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition This is a very complete kit and does contain everything you need to setup a Raspberry Pi 3. Yes, the op system installs easily and, with luck, you can be up and running in less than an hour. So, why the 2 stars?

It gets 2 stars because the Raspberry Pi is probably one of the most frustrating devices I've ever tried to put to any real use. For example, I wanted to set it up so I could use a VNC server on the Pi and a VNC client on my Mac (OS X El Capitan). After three days of almost non-stop failures, I'm sick of this thing. Researching how to get this task done leads you down a black hole of internet articles and posts on the Raspberry Pi site, most of that give different instructions, use different commands, tell you which files to edit and what to put in them, and almost none work, period!

The core problem rests squarely on the Raspberry Pi organization. Their own website is full of conflicting posts on how to do just about anything beyond a basic setup. Few, if any posts state which model of Pi is being referenced, and many bear no date. All in all, it's a very frustrating experience and, while I like to tinker with these things, a little success is required once in a while to keep me chugging along. I think I'm done with this thing. I had hoped it would finally be a Linux for the rest of us. Unfortunately, it's just as convoluted and difficult to use as any version of Linux out there (my opinion).

However, if you're looking to explore the Pi, this kit has everything you need to do a basic setup of Linux. And, should you want to use it as a web server, file server, media server, you're really on your own. Drink lots of coffee and plan to pull our lots of hair.
text_fidelity_b: CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White Black Friday sales have brought the Echo Dot to under $30, and that is how I am now buying my second one.

So yes, often times you do need to formulate your requests in a certain way (for instance, try asking Alexa how much time it will take to go to work... I gave up on this...) and enunciate them more clearly if you missed, but in general, this technology is just amazing.
Sometimes I even ask Alexa for information I don't need, just for fun.

I like that they named it Alexa. That's so much better than "Okay Google." It feels like a real person. Who in hell at Google thought it's a good idea to force users to use their company name, and thus remind them that their huge creepy analytics private data gathering network is behind it?

Possible improvements:
* Bring back the matte finish from 1st gen. I shouldn't have to pay more to not have it shiny...
* Listen to the word "stop" when the alarm is ringing. Currently you need to wait until it's not ringing and then say "Alexa, stop."
* Add confirmation and modification prompts to "Add a new event to the calendar." Currently if she misunderstood one word, you have to start all over again.
* Alexa bluntly tells you that she cannot tell you about the events in your calendar on a specific date... C'mon guys...
* Implement the word "Repeat": sometimes you didn't hear or didn't catch the information you were looking for, and currently you have to formulate your request again
* Only gives info about the last Amazon order. She can retrieve more order but you have to be very specific about what they contain.
* I wish Alexa could Google more stuff.
* Choose your own wake up word

I never use Siri on my iPhone, but for some reason it feels very natural to use Alexa, maybe because the device is more "fixed" whereas my phone could be in a backpack, in the other room...

The Killer App is MUSIC. We have an Echo Dot in the bedroom, and my wife just loves to ask Alexa for tunes. We have it linked to Spotify.

Also, I am a software engineer, and I have added some custom features through my own skills. I wish somebody came up with something simple to add your own skills, because this is really useful. For instance, the bus comes in front of my house at the most random times, so I developed a skill that tells me in how many minutes the next buses will come. So much faster than having to check a website on my phone!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

Amazon Kindle 9W PowerFast Adapter for Accelerated Charging I purchased this to go along with my new 8.9 inch Fire HD (and I'm counting the days until it arrives), but it also works with the original Fire. I found the major benefit for the original Fire to be the better form factor -- unlike the "wart" shape of the original Fire charger, this is much more sleek, with folding plugs to make it very easy to carry in a case. Very simple, clean design.

The downside to using it with the original Fire is that you need to provide your own cable from the charger to the Fire, as the charger does NOT include it.

The charge time is only slightly faster for the original Fire. Using the app Battery HD to measure charge time and level, the new charger saved about 15 minutes to go from a 15% charge to a 100% charge versus the original charger. Faster, but not a huge gain. I expect that the differential in terms of charge time for the new Fire (especially the 8.9 inch one) will be much greater when comparing this charger with using a USB port to charge. I'll post results once I have my 8.9 inch Fire.

While it's not a compelling purchase if you have the original Fire, it is worth getting (at 50% off) if ordered with a new HD Fire, especially if you can also get the MP3 credit. I'm giving it 5-stars since, at the price paid, it's very handy to have as a spare charger, and it's MUCH easier to take along than the original Fire charger.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle 9W PowerFast Adapter for Accelerated Charging

text_fidelity_a:
Damero 2pcs/Set Portable Electronic Accessories Travel Organizer, Black I'll admit it right up front: I am an organizer junkie. I love having all of my things laid out perfectly and well organized in all of the different areas of my house. While I try to minimize as much as possible, if I do need to have a variety of items, and let's face it, electronics accessories and cords seem to multiply like rabbits, I want to keep them in an organized, attractive way so that I can always find what I'm looking for and so that they look nice on my shelves.

This two-piece set is meant to be a travel organizer kit for your electronics, but I'm using it in my office to keep all of the excess cords, cards, plugs, etc. for all of my various peripherals. It's fabulous, because I have one that I keep near my computer and one that I keep in my closet, depending on the frequency of use. If I need to get a cord out, it's right there, yet the cases are subtle enough that I don't feel like I'm looking at something overly functional all the time. It just looks neat, clean, and well-planned.

The quality on these is amazing. They are just stiff enough to hold their shape, yet flexible enough that if something's a little bit taller I can close the zipper over it and it's no big deal. The dividers attached by Velcro and so you can move them around so that it works perfectly around whatever it is you want to store and there. text_fidelity_a: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop First let me say that I grew up typing on actual typewriters and I find myself getting really nostalgic about those days the older I get.  Not that I mind sleek, modern keyboards.  I do a great deal of writing, so I have adapted to the various styles as they've come out.  This particular keyboard is nice and pleasant to work on, but I wouldn't say it's a true typewriter style experience.  The keys are too flat and too round for that.  If you are like me and you do a lot of typing and can adapt yourself quickly between different keyboards you will probably enjoy this one.  I do find myself making a lot of typos that I normally wouldn't when I'm working on it though.  The mouse is honestly just annoying.  There is no actual switch to turn it off, just a button right on top that seems to 'wake' it when it goes dormant, so if you're prone to bumping it around or accidentally dropping things on it or if you plan on using it in multiple places for any reason whatsoever you will find yourself getting frustrated with just how easy it is to turn it back on.  The scroll wheel is fantastic, but the one on my previous mouse no longer works at all, so that might be the reason why I like it so much.  The accuracy of its tracking leaves a lot to be desired and it's quite loud when you click it, but I do tend to prefer to keep my environment quiet.  All in all I would not purchase this again both because the keyboard design is just 'off' in enough nit-picky ways to make it frustrating (so many typos) and because the mouse tracking and lack of a true 'off' switch makes it frustrating to actually use it.  Both the keyboard and the mouse are really pretty to look at and well built for what they are, but I wouldn't call them truly functional even though they do work.  If you're just doing minor browsing and not a lot of typing they would be fine for that, but if you're someone that does a lot of writing or anything that requires precision tracking of the mouse like playing games or working in paint programs you should probably skip this set.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop

text_fidelity_a:
Mad Catz R.A.T. 7 Albino Edition Professional Gaming Mouse The Rat 7 mouse seems to be going for the customization market, but where it really excels is in simple build quality. The weight, smooth precision parts, and mechanical functioning of this mouse make it feel less like a peripheral and more like a piece of tactical combat gear. The buttons are well placed, the macro customization is deep, it slides smoothly without catching, and the sensor does its job very well.

My gripes are mostly minor. Just about everything on this mouse is movable or can be switched out for alternate parts, even the weight and balance are adjustable, but I found that as much as I wanted to use the grippy parts in some places, they just didn't feel right, while the slick pieces are awesome. There are two small hex bolts that I find to be unfortunately placed. One rests right under your thumb, and the other under whichever finger you hold on the right of the mouse. They aren't uncomfortable, and may even help orient your hand position, but I find they break up the otherwise smooth feel of the mouse. The action on the scroll wheel and button clicks are very nice. My one criticism on the sensor is that the hole is very small and tends to collect small lint particles that can interfere with the sensing.

The only time I find myself hitting buttons on accident is when picking up the mouse, I often hit the forward and back buttons, which can be irritating in web pages, but can always be remapped. There is a really well placed little red button above the thumb that triggers a fine tuned aiming mode. As much as I like the feature, I'd really like to be able to map this button to something else on occasion, but haven't found an option to do so.

Everything you need to do with the mouse, you can access from the mouse. The tools for adjustment are built in, the button for changing between function sets is accessible, but hard to hit on accident, and changes color with mode. Perhaps my favorite feature on the Rat 7 is the small rocker switch behind the scroll wheel which can be used to raise and lower the mouse sensitivity (pointer speed) on the fly, which nearly makes the precision aim button obsolete.

I'm used to using an ambidextrous mouse and switching hands often. This mouse can be used left handed without much difficulty, but you lose access to some of the buttons and features when doing so, most notably the horizontal scroll. Overall a very nice purchase and I'm quite pleased with it. More than worth the price difference between it and the lesser mice on the market.
text_fidelity_b: Mad Catz R.A.T. 7 Albino Edition Professional Gaming Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(

Wacom Bamboo Pen Tablet After one month of using my Wacom Bamboo Pen which I purchased at Amazon.com I am happy to say that it corrected my repetitive injury (carpal tunnel), and the artwork that I am able to produce now is much closer to the natural form that I am used to in the real world (pencil and paper). I coupled my Wacom pen along with Ubuntu 10.10 and a fantastic application that was developed around the Wacom pen called "MyPaint". I am now very productive in my pursuit as an artist in perfecting my art and I could not be more pleased with this product. For those that wish to try Ubuntu and MyPaint this how you get them...

Since Ubuntu is a free Linux distribution based on the GNU/Linux Debian you can download it free at [...] You can also get the Wacom Bamboo Pen to work by copying and pasting the code below into a terminal within Ubuntu...

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:doctormo/wacom-plus
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install wacom-dkms

Reboot your system and your Wacom Bamboo Pen will be fully functional. Now, to install "MyPaint"...

sudo apt-get install mypaint

No need to reboot after that you will find the application under Applications>Graphics>MyPaint

Enjoy! your Wacom Bamboo Pen. You not only got a great deal from the wonderful people at Amazon.com who sold it to you below the suggested retail price but, if you followed the instructions above and got Ubuntu running on your computer, as well as installing "MyPaint" you have a complete art studio which will serve you well in exploring many things you can achieve using your Wacom Bamboo Pen.

Have a great day! :-)
text_fidelity_b: Wacom Bamboo Pen Tablet

text_fidelity_a:
woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue PROS

1. The silicone band is very comfortable. Apparently if it breaks, it can be replaced, though I’m not sure where or how you would buy a new band.

2. The appearance is sleek and modern, and the size of the watch face makes the digital numbers easy to read.

3. It has a rechargeable battery, which may have a longer life than the non-rechargeable batteries of most sports watches.

4. If you want a smart watch that is far cheaper than most brands, this might work for you.

CONS

1. There are three primary functions that I use a sports watch for: to instantly check the time, a stopwatch, and a timer. It irritated me no end with this watch that, after only a few seconds of being lit up, its face goes dark. While this might save the charge on the rechargeable battery, there are plenty of times when my right hand it not free to punch the button on this watch to light up its face, and I can’t quickly and conveniently check the time! It is also a hassle trying to use the stopwatch and timer functions.

2. I absolutely loathe the way this watch’s battery is recharged. Instead of using a standard C cable, the charging cable attaches magnetically, and it becomes detached far too easily. There is also no warning when the battery of this watch is about to go dead.

3. I don’t like the software this phone uses. It is a major hassle to learn for what I personally consider very little useful return. Why? Because most of the functions offered by this watch that are of any interest to me I can get through my smartphone. I use my phone and a Bluetooth for phone calls, texting, music, and hearing alarms. I check the weather by looking around me when outside or looking at weather apps on my phone. I use my phone for photography.
The rest of the functions this watch offers I personally find to be useless. I do not need a watch to tell me how to do a deep breathing exercises. As a healthy individual with no heart issues, I do not need to monitor my heart rate 24/7. (And if I did, I would use medical equipment that is far more reliable than this cheap watch.) I don’t need to obsessively monitor my sleep. (And, again, if I did, I wouldn’t trust this cheap watch to do an accurate job of it.)

4. Its pedometer function might have been of use to me, but unfortunately, it is inaccurate.

CONCLUSION

I dumped this watch and went back to a regular, inexpensive sports watch.
text_fidelity_b: woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch This is a retro leather laptop messenger bag - the material is made from something called "Buffalo" leather, which feels rough and stiff - quite the opposite of lambskin or buttery soft leather. The buckles are only for show because you can open and close the bag without unbuckling it, as there are buttons underneath. It has a weathered look, with varying shades of brown and sienna that give the impression that you're an Indiana Jones-type adventurer who's been carrying this bag through the outback, escaped tigers and bears, and came through fine, though the bag is a bit battered.

In other words, it's very manly, and harks back to the 1940s when bulky items were the norm because thinner materials hadn't been invented yet. While it looks great and seems well made (it's from India), it's actually limited in terms of actual everyday use. If you're traveling a lot, you want things to be as lightweight as possible. This is not one of those items. Even when empty, it feels cumbersome to carry. Stuffed with a laptop and papers, it will be heavy.

Think about it - when was the last time you actually saw someone on the train or airport carrying one of these? You might say you'd like to do so because it will make you look unique. In reality, other people may have tried carrying one of these and gave up.

So while it's nice as a conversation piece and something you might want to show off to your friends, I fear it will be one of those novelty items that, after its newness has worn off, will be relegated to the back of the closet.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch

text_fidelity_a:
DUOTEN IPX7 Waterproof Speaker, Portable Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Speaker with Suction Cup Shower Speaker, Longer Playtime RGB Lights, 360° Surround Sound Rich Bass for Outdoors, Travel, Pool, Beach My computer speakers kept going out on me every now and then, so I wanted this speaker to take their place. It will also be good for using with my projector, as its sound is not very loud. I tried listening to music on it from my phone first, and it sounds pretty good, though it could use more bass, especially for music.
Maybe, it's because I grew up in the 80s era, when there was real music and it had lots of bass, and I still want a lot of it. This speaker just doesn't have quite enough for me, but I still really like it. It is a bit taller and skinnier than a couple of older echo dots, and it doesn't have the same exact quality of sound, but sounds pretty darn good.
The color-changing light effect is pretty cool, but I wish there was a way to turn it off sometimes. Because I'm using it as a computer speaker most of the day, and it's a bit bothersome.
This little speaker packs a pretty good punch, aside from needing a bit more bass, and not being able to turn the light off. It will work great for times when you need a pretty loud sound source and have little room for a big speaker. It's small, has a slot for an SD card for playing your own playlist, it's rechargeable, and lasts for a good while before needing to be recharged. I would definitely recommend it!
text_fidelity_b: DUOTEN IPX7 Waterproof Speaker, Portable Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Speaker with Suction Cup Shower Speaker, Longer Playtime RGB Lights, 360° Surround Sound Rich Bass for Outdoors, Travel, Pool, Beach

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Leather Case, Onyx Black - fits all Paperwhite generations prior to 2018 (Will not fit All-new Paperwhite 10th generation) After being a NOOK user for just over a year, I fell in love with the Kindle Paperwhite, decided to switch platforms, and joined the Kindle family in February. After using the Kindle for about a week without a cover, I felt I needed to protect my new device. I bought two cases from third party vendors, and they were just okay. My Paperwhite seemed to float around inside these cases, so I bit the bullet and bought Amazon's leather cover in Fuchsia. When I received it, I wasn't thrilled with the color, so I returned it and got Onyx Black instead. While I love it--it's very stylish, elegant, and the border blends perfectly with the device--my Kindle also kept blending in with other tech gadgets around the house that live in black cases. I went to Best Buy and looked at the case in Royal Purple (in my area, they only sell Onyx Black, Fuchsia, and Royal Purple), but again I didn't care for that color either. On a whim, I ordered the Persimmon case, which I got yesterday. I'm very happy!!! It is a beautiful coral color, not what the Amazon website depicts, but also not a true red, and the trim accentuates the Kindle perfectly. I don't find it distracting. I have been so happy with this case that I paid the extra $20 to turn off Special Offers and it works as advertised. The Kindle sits perfectly flush inside, closes flush, and even when I fold the front cover back there's no floating (very distracting when you're reading and the Kindle "shifts" when you move your finger to turn a page). Anyway, I'll be selling the Onyx Black case, which is, after one month of use, in excellent condition. I highly, highly recommend these cases for the Kindle Paperwhite, and if you like cheerful, bright colors, go with Persimmon. The only cons I can think of are: there should have been a teal and green option, and I wish the inside of the front cover had the Kindle logo engraved on it (don't think that's a lot to ask for the price; instead the inside logo feels like it was ironed on).
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Leather Case, Onyx Black - fits all Paperwhite generations prior to 2018 (Will not fit All-new Paperwhite 10th generation)

text_fidelity_a:
Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver After an attempt to use [[ASIN:B005INJ4ZG My Zone Wireless Headphones]] was a bust for me due to its terrible sound quality, my techie husband bought this amp for me as part of a setup that allows me to listen to TV as loud as I want without disturbing him or the neighbors.

I directly hook up this amp to a head phone or earbuds when I am sitting close to the TV by using a special [[ASIN:B00009UVPN adapter]]. Head phones and earbuds have a 1/8 inch (3.5 mm) male jack (AKA male connector). Without an adapter, they can't be inserted into this amp, whose plug (AKA socket, female jack, or female connector) measures 1/4 inch (6.35 mm).

Because I like to move around my living room when I am watching TV, my husband also bought me a special [[ASIN:B0010CX798 male-to-female, headphone adapter, extension cable]]. The 1/4-inch, male jack of this cable fits into the 1/4-inch plug of this amp, and it has a 1/8-inch plug on its other end into which the jack of a head phone or ear bud can fit.

In order to use this setup, my husband also hooked into this amp a [[ASIN:B000068O3F male-to-male extension cable]]; one end is 1/8-inch and the other is 1/4-inch in diameter. The smaller end fits into a plug on the TV. When I want to use this external speaker source, I use the TV remote to access a menu that allows me to do that. Once this system is hooked up, I can no longer adjust the sound volume on the TV itself. I use the volume control on this amp.

Note that there is no On/Off switch on this amp. If you want to turn it off, so that you are not wasting electricity when it is not in use, you unhook the power cord from the far-left side of the amp.

This setup is a little complicated for the non-techie to figure out on their own, but if you have anyone techie in your family who can do it for you, it works really well.
text_fidelity_b: Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver

Sony MDRV6 Studio Monitor Headphones with CCAW Voice Coil I record interview audio for video/DSLR shoots professionally. My go-to system begins with a Sennheiser MKH416-T short shotgun mic into a Sound Devices 302 mixer (which can power the T-power mic), the line-in into a JuicedLink RM222 then into a Nikon D800, then recording to the HDMI output to an Atomos Ninja.

To monitor, I plug my trusty MDRV6's into the monitor out of the 302 mixer, which is listening via its return to the headphone output of the Nikon. With a knob turn, I can then listen to any of the mixer's three inputs directly or to the camera's return confidence feed.

If it sounds good in the Sony MDRV6's, it'll sound good in the edit.

Yes, there are way more expensive headphones, but I know how the MDRV6's sound, I trust them, and they never break.

The biggest problem is coworkers "borrowing" them and not returning them. Write your name on them in large letters.

For it's size it rocked out in my back porch. Due to the IP64 rating it's a bit heavy but that's a good thing.

I tested this speaker paired with a Sony android phone. Bluetooth pairing was instant. While I didn't quite get a full 30 foot range, I found the actual 27 foot range to be acceptable.

I dropped the speaker from my waist height of 36" onto the concrete pad on my porch. No issues with playability or broken pieces. Although I did notice a slight scuff mark. No biggie.

I like the carabiner feature for hanging the speaker, from a tent ceiling, tree, or post. But I don't see anyone hanging the speaker off a backpack. The weight will cause it to swing wildly. In fact it's heavy enough to be stored in the bottom of your pack.

Recharging was easy, but the rubber plug takes a little finesse to put it back into place.

The sound was crisp with somewhat deep bass undertones. I didn't expect this little speaker to pump out heavy bass, but it's adequate for its size.

I don't recommend that you crank this up too loud when camping in the woods. The loud music might drown out the sounds of an attacking bear or wildebeest.

For the money it's a decent wireless speaker that will survive most outdoor adventures.

text_fidelity_a:
Magellan RoadMate 1470 4.7-Inch Widescreen Portable GPS Navigator I've been a Magellan user for several years - have owned four of their GPS systems, and always appreciate how they have improved their products. This unit is my 5th, and replaces a Magellan 4040. After using it for a while I've confident in saying this is the best one yet!

The most visible change is the actual size of the unit. The screen size has been increased, but the unit is thinner and lighter. Very sleek appearance, and the screen is a real joy -- sharp, clear graphics even in the sun, and bigger on-screen buttons for easy use. The mounting system has also been streamlined, and looks and works well. It mounts very easily on a NavMat holder (basically a bean-bag system that I got on Amazon. I'm a huge Navmat fan - makes it a snap to hide the GPS with narry a trace. Best accessory by far for any GPS).

The power connector was not well thought out, however. You have to connect it to the GPS unit AFTER you mount it in the holder. They should have moved the connector it a wee bit to the side to avoid that.

The only button is a slide-type power button on the top. Boot-up time is OK -- not speedy, but not a huge delay either. It does not have a "sleep" mode, so you have to do a cold boot every time. Not a problem in real world use - by the time you get situated in your car, the unit is ready to go.

Voice is clear and easy to understand. Not as natural sounding as a TomTom, but understandable.

Pretty much any recent GPS unit will get you where you want to go. I've found the routing on the Magellans to be very similar to Garmins - could be because they both use the same mapping set (Navteq). The Magellan shines, however, in features that I find helpful. The direction of the next turn is always visible regardless of how far away the next turn will be. Up until recently, Garmin did not offer this (they do now on some of their units). Sounds like a small issue, but I find it very helpful. The Magellan also allows you to very easily exclude a route (or portion). That's a fairly standard feature nowadays, but Magellan allows you to do it in a snap.

In terms of routing, Magellan offers four options (fastest, shortest, most use of freeways and least use). You can see all four options on the map (as a summary) at the same time so you can pick the best one for your needs. Perfect!!

Love the AAA Guidebook, which is a unique Magellan feature. Lets you get details about restaurants and other points of interest just like the paper version from AAA. I used it a lot in my 4040, especially when traveling out of town.

Other unique Magellan features I appreciate is the "ding dong" sound right before a turn (incredibly accurate!) and the fact that the software reminds you to "stay on the current road" when you encounter major exits. Some find that to be nagging, but it has saved me from inadvertently exiting on more than one occasion.

A new feature for Magellan is the lane guidance. Very nicely done. I've used this feature on Navigon units, and found it rather unhelpful. Magellan's implementation is far more useful, with better, clearer graphics. However, lane guidance is not available for every road.

The software is also nicely done - very logical to use. If you're a past Magellan user you can pick this up and use it in a second. If not, there's a short printed user's guide in the box (plus a CD-ROM with more in-depth info) that gets you up to speed quickly. The box also includes the mount, power connector for the car, and a USB cable. It does not include an AC adapter.

OK, now for the bad news. When it comes to customer service, Magellan has been horrid. We're talking so bad it's almost funny. I'm hoping this situation will change - the company was bought by Mitac late last year, and perhaps this will signal a change for the better in terms of customer support. Lord knows, they couldn't get any worse.

The leader, in my opinion, for customer support is Garmin. They are nice to deal with on the phone, answer emails promptly, and offer regular firmware updates. Whenever I buy a GPS as a gift I always buy Garmin since I don't want to saddle the recipient with the miserable service that Magellan offers. It's a shame, since Magellan offers some real benefits over Garmin, and more value for the money. Tom Tom is also decent when it comes to support, but they use TeleAtlas maps which are less complete than NavTeq (sp?).

Bottom line -- if you're looking for a straightforward GPS at a good price, this should be on your short list. It lacks features such as Bluetooth and an MP3 player, but for me, I want a GPS to offer guidance and not entertainment. This has a very robust feature set, great screen, and well-designed software. It also has traffic capabilities -- did not test that feature out, so I can't comment on it.

The "safe" bet continues to be Garmin. You'll pay a bit more, and get less features, but you can be assured of solid support. Whether Magellan's new owners will put them back on the right track (if you'll excuse the horrid, but unavoidable pun) in terms of customer service is not yet clear. I hope so -- they make a great product!

UPDATE: 5/21/09 There's a firmware update on the Magellan site. No new functionality (in terms of new features) but, according to the release notes it improves overall performance. Easy to install - just follow the included step-by-step instructions. It seems like it makes the unit a bit faster, but that could just be my imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Magellan RoadMate 1470 4.7-Inch Widescreen Portable GPS Navigator

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate BlackArmor NAS 220 2-Bay 2TB (2 x 1 TB) Network Attached Storage ST320005LSA10G-RK I needed something bigger than my external hard drive to back up my files on my home computer which runs on Windows XP. I'm just about of space and all I want to do is to move stuff from my computer to the Black Armor NAS data server. Looks like it just ain't gonna happen.

After finally getting the program to install I get to where I'm ready to transfer data. Everything is correctly hooked up hardware speaking. After clicking on the "Black Armor Backup" icon on my desktop I get to this point:

It asks: "What would you like to do?" I click on "Backup".
It says: "Data to backup selection" I click on "My Computer"

I click on the teeny tiny box in upper left hand corner that says "Disk 1". It automatically checks NTFS and FAT32.
I click on "next".

It gives me 2 options: to "Create New Backup Archive" or "Add to Existing Backup Archive". It has automatically selected "Create New Backup Archive" which is what I want since this is the first time I'm backing up my computer.

In the "Backup Location Box" I see a few numbers and letters plus the "browse" box. The "next" button is greyed out so I have to do something here...hhmmmm...
So I click on "Browse" and Click on "Download on Seagate Black Armor NAS".
Then apparently I'm supposed to generate a name though it already has one in the box.
I click on "Generate a Name" and the name in the box changes by adding "\Download\My Backup.tib
I click "O.K."

Then: The file name, location or format"\\blah\Download \MyBackup.tib" is not valid.
Please type the file name or location in the correct format.
(I've gotten several different error messages at this point, but somehow it later lets me go the blue box.)

It goes to a small blue box asking user name and password.
I type in the username and password that the paper sheet in the box which came with the NAS told me to use.
And then I get an error message saying exactly the following:

"\\generated name| Download is not accessible. You might not have permission to use this network resource. Contact the administrator of this server to find out if you have access permissions.

Multiple connections to a server or shared resource by the same user, using more than one user name, are not allowed. Disconnect all previous connections to the server or shared resource and try again.

O.K."

So, I'm not anywhere near being a technical expert at this stuff. All I want to do is move some data from box A to box B so that Box A has a lot more room to work with. I've wasted a lot of time messing with this and nowhere in the PDF manual can I find the solution. I got this for free from Vine so it's going back in the box and in the closet. I'm reconnecting my other external hard drive which never gives me problems.

July 28th - I had to uninstall BlackArmor software. It made it very difficult to boot my computer. I got a fuzzy gray/blue screen with BLACKARMOR plastered all over it. My mouse would not work properly. I could only go up and down if I moved my mouse back and forth horizontally. This was just too unnerving.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate BlackArmor NAS 220 2-Bay 2TB (2 x 1 TB) Network Attached Storage ST320005LSA10G-RK

Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case These headphones are advertised more for business use than for music. The business features do work great. There is a bluetooth adapter included in the package so you can use the headphones with PCs that don't have built-in bluetooth. You can connect the headphones to 2 different bluetooth sources simultaneously so you can have a Skype call on your laptop and connect to your smartphone at the same time. There is a nice pass-through mode that lets you listen to your surroundings (or not) by pushing a button on the Jabra app.

Speaking of the app, the included manual is very skimpy and really unnecessary. To use these headphones you should download the Jabra app to your phone or PC and use the app to pair and configure the headphones. Many of the features are only available through the app.

Sound quality of the headphone is great for business use, very solid with no connection problems. For music, this is not the best I have heard from "true wireless" headphones. Some music-focused "true wireless" headphones that I own have better clarity and detail. The Jabra app does have an equalizer feature, but the effect is more subtle than what I get from other headphones.

These headphones are very comfortable and very secure, actually surprisingly secure for headphones that don't have any wings or clips. 3 different size ear tips are included, though no memory foam tips like you get with some headphones in this price range.

Battery life is 5 hours per charge and you can recharge twice with the included carrying case. That's good for "true wireless" headphones.

I would give these headphones 5 stars if the sound quality was better. It does have good business features and those are the main focus of this product. Bluetooth connection is very solid and build quality is great. 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65t True Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds, UC Optimized – Superior Call Quality and Connectivity – Passive Noise Cancelling Earbuds with up to 15 hours of Battery Life with Charging Case

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin 8-Outlet AV Power Strip Surge Protector with 6-Foot Power Cord and 2 USB Charging Ports, 3000 Joules, Black (BV108050-06-BLK) I love that this surge protector and plug strip has two USB ports for charging my Kindle and cell phone, but the placement of the USB ports, which is a major selling point for this unit, is hindered by the position of the cord wrap feature as well as the areas to plug in your larger electronics that have the big boxy plug. The USB ports are tucked right in between the cord wrap spot and the place to plug in larger plugs, so if one isn't blocking your USB ports, the other is.

In addition, I kind of wish that the majority of the plugs were spaced farther apart. I have a few electronics that have very small boxy plugs, and those don't fit right next to one another on the main area of the plug strip. The only thing that will fit on those plugs without overlapping are the traditional small plugs that are on lamps and other uncomplicated items. I don't have too many of those, and I'm guessing that most people buy plug strips because they have a bunch of electronics, almost all of which would have those bigger boxy plugs.

That said, the surge protector feature is absolutely effective, and I know this because we had PG&E replacing some poles in our neighborhood recently and we had many incidences of brownouts, surges, and spotty power, and this unit kept any harm from coming to any of my electronics that were plugged into it.

And while it is easy to make design suggestions, I have to say that I haven't found the perfect plug strip yet. Almost all of them seem to have some design characteristics that make them not quite ideal. While this unit is not perfectly designed with regards to the placement of the USB ports and the spacing of the regular plugs, it is certainly a high-quality, very functional unit that does what it says it does, and I trust the Belkin brand that it's going to function for some time. This plug strip is also nice in that it has a space so that you can mount it on the wall or on the back of your desk if you so desire.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 8-Outlet AV Power Strip Surge Protector with 6-Foot Power Cord and 2 USB Charging Ports, 3000 Joules, Black (BV108050-06-BLK)

I'm a technical trail runner and not a triathlete, so this watch will see outdoor use 12 months a year in all manner of Midwest weather, and the only water would be a shower or a soak in the hot tub lol.
I like the design, as a round face seems more like a watch than a tracker, and that's was about it. The band feels like it'll break each time I take it off or put on. The "Side Swipe" feature was being triggered when I would flex my wrist or during random movements. Tried switching it from righty to lefty. Still no good, so I turned that feature off. Now the side button has been triggered numerous times when lifting or sleeping. I've woken up several times to the GPS being triggered while I was tossing or turning, and drained a majority of the battery life. Which brings me to another issue. Two short runs of an hour each on successive days drain the battery from 100% to under 15%, which is ridiculous. The previous Garmin was good for at least 3 solid runs before needing a charge, and this won't go 2 days. This is going back this week, and may try to bag a Fenix 5 on sale at AMZN in the future. GPS was solid, as it's a Garmin after all, but after that, I'm not pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-01769-01 Vivoactive 3, GPS Smartwatch with Contactless Payments and Built-In Sports Apps, Black with Silver Hardware

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer I've had the Harmony One remote since the day it came out, and now "upgraded" to the Harmony Ultimate Remote.

Build and Setup:
This is a very solid remote. It is heavy for its size with clean lines and elegant design. Inside the box is the powered hub with two remote blasters, remote, base, and power cords for the hub and the base. There does not appear to be a removable battery like with the Harmony One.

Set up was very simple. As I already had my settings in myremotesetup.com, I simply had to log into myharmony.com, transfer my settings to the new remote and the remote was setup. It was very easy.

The difference between this remote and other Harmony remotes is that this has a hub and blaster units that connects through your wireless network to allow you to connect and control your units with your smartphone.

You have to connect the hub and blaster units around the units you want to control. It has to be connected to your home wireless network, which was easy. You can either do it through myharmony.com or by pressing the setup button on the hub and your router (if it supports it) it was that easy.

I have my hub on the shelf with my Blu Ray, Dish Box, and Xbox. The one blaster is near the television, and the other is on another shelf with my Wii and my surround sound box. When you go into advanced settings on your remote you tell the remote to control the devices with either just the remote, with the hub, blaster 1, blaster 2, or all of them. This allows flexibility where you setup and place your devices and blaster and hub units.

Using the Remote:
The remote is easy to use. Many of the major buttons; play, pause, fast forward, volume and such are hard buttons on the remote. The remote has a large touch screen that can do all the other device options you may seem fit to try. It scrolls across several pages: Home screen allows you to choose between actions such as watch tv or dvd, channel favorites (which you program), current action screen that controls actions related to what you are doing, and finally the number screen, here is where you can enter numbers to change channels. This last part is a bit of a pain as when I am channel surfing I like to be able to press number buttons to change channels and you really can't do this with this remote without looking.

To operate DVR like functions you can also swipe up from any screen to access a black screen where you can program gestures. By default you press to pause, swipe right to skip forward, swipe right to swipe back, etc.

Phone App:
The phone app for the android is a bit lacking as it is not quite as sophisticated as the remote itself, but can do most of the actions of the remote as long as you are connected to the same wireless network as your hub is.

Troubleshooting:
The remote is easy to use and troubleshoot, Simply rebooting or re-syncing the remote can resolve most problems I've found. It also prompts you for assistance the first time you add an action or new device.

Overall this is a great remote. This will demand, though, some knowledge on your part as it is a very sophisticated remote. Many problems that occur can easily be resolved by some knowledge of networks, remotes, or Harmony devices in general. If you have experience with this you will enjoy the functions and capacity of this remote.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
Turtle Beach Recon 70 Multiplatform Gaming Headset for Xbox Series X| S, Xbox One, PS5, PS4, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, Mobile, & PC with 3.5mm-Flip-to-Mute Mic, 40mm Speakers-Blue Camo I got these for my 7yr old who kept wanting to use my Sennheiser's. After about the fourth time he dropped them and/or tried to walk off with them still on his head I decided it was time for kiddo to get his own headset. I was skeptical of these, due to the low price, but the reviews were decent.. and he's a menace, so figured I'd see.

Pros:
*Price, they are wonderfully priced for what they provide
*Mic is crystal clear, his voice comes across bit higher pitched but he's 7 its not like it was all that low to begin with.
*Flip up mic to mute. I love this feature, I have it on my Senn's and I'm not sure I could do with out it. If you hate push to talk, then you want a flip to mute mic. Unless you like to entertain discord with your drama.
*They are adjustable to the point that both my kid and my husband fit them comfortably.
*Volume adjust is on the earpiece, I hate trying to find it on the cord, this is much more convenient. Now I just have to convince him that he needs to keep the volume at a safe low level. His headphones for school are for kids and had a volume limiter. I see why now.

Cons:
*The connector cable is old school rubberized plastic (rather than the more durable braided cord).
*Connector is also super short, no way he is using them on a docked Switch
*They feel a bit flimsy and plastic, however this also makes the light which is nice
*Thin on the padding across the headpiece, although the ear cups are comfortable enough
*Ear cups are on the smaller size. They were fine for everyone in our household, but if you have issues with headsets and your ears you will probably have them with this set.

As a neither pro or con, these only block some outside sound. I wouldn't say they are open or close, but somewhere in between. He can still hear me yell at him from the other room which is nice, but I do have to yell. Sound is lacking in substantial bass, but at this price they are all going to be. For a gaming headset under $50, the sound is crisp and clear, as was the mic.

TL;DR If you are on a budget or just don't want to see an expensive pair get destroyed (kids, dogs, etc) I highly recommend these. I did ding a star though for the cord, they say they are for the Switch and I just don't see how a docked switch could use these.
text_fidelity_b: Turtle Beach Recon 70 Multiplatform Gaming Headset for Xbox Series X| S, Xbox One, PS5, PS4, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch, Mobile, & PC with 3.5mm-Flip-to-Mute Mic, 40mm Speakers-Blue Camo

Arctic Silver 5: 64-65° max
Kryonaut: 66-67° max.

The fact that I used this paste on both my laptop and desktop, and have also re applied the paste multiple times, leads me to believe that I am using the paste right (since AS5 performs better, *consistently*). And instead that the Kryonaut that I got is fake or a bad batch.
