text_fidelity_a:
Razer Deathadder Infrared Gaming Mouse Okay, so Razer has a reputation for making products that are of low quality or break prematurely. There may be some truth to that. The "back" button double and triple clicks. I am going to replace the switch.

There is an LED lighted scroll wheel which feels of quality. The sides are a hard smooth plastic. The rest the body is coated with a rubber-like material. There is a lighted Razer logo and I turned off all the LED's.

Even though there is a problem with my mouse I decided to keep it and fix the problem. I have to say that this is probably the most ergonomic, comfortable mouse I have ever used. It has a very high arch and is shaped for a palm grip. I personally don't know if it would be a good gaming mouse ever. The sides are VERY slippery and if you needed a lot of control I don't know if you would have it. Especially if you had to lift off the mouse to readjust, it may slip. In my opinion the Roccat XTD Kone is the best mouse I have ever used. It is very big and heavy and there are grooves for your thumb and outer fingers. It feels more sturdy.

The reason I gave it 3 stars instead of 4, the mouse is always a little warm to the touch and it seems to absorb heat from your hand and get hotter. The Roccat mouse is made from similar materials and always feels cool. I have heard that there are parts of the circuitry that generate more heat than normal. So in summary, I like it for general use. If I was gaming or doing something that requires precision such as graphic design I would use the Roccat Kone XTD.

Edit: follow up- I have owned this mouse now for 3 weeks and I have it next to the Roccat mouse. I should share that I have used the Razer almost exclusively and switched to the Roccat only when I needed to use forward and back buttons (they are hard to reach on Razer). I think the Razer is more comfortable to rest your hand on for long periods at a time. However, it just seems that I have better control of the right click, left click, and forward-back buttons. The DA causes your hand to form an arch, while your hand is more flat with the Roccat. I wonder if your index finger is in a stronger postion with the Roccat; it feels so.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Deathadder Infrared Gaming Mouse

Belkin DuraTek Plus USB Lightning Cable - USB-A Cable with Leather Strap - Ultra-Strong Charging Cable With Flexible Insulation - Compatible with iPhone, iPad, Airpods and More - 4ft/1.2m (White) I have gone through multiple chargers throughout my life. I tend to not follow the advice of "Protect your phone's battery and your charger cable by not using your phone while it's charging!!" What can I say, I'm a rebel. Because of this, my chargers don't last very long. I've had about a week of consistent use for the 4ft version of this one and I am really enjoying it. I have a few pros and one con.
The positives:
-The cable feels incredibly sturdy in your hands. It would take a lot for it to start ripping or breaking.
-I tested the charging capacity with multiple reciprocals to see if it effected the charge. As expected, the charging capacity depends solely on the power it is provided with, which is great!
-The length is manageable without being too much. Anything 6ft or longer tends to be flaky. This 4ft is absolutely fantastic in my opinion.
-The lightning adapter plugs into my phone easier than the Apple branded one that came with my phone so that was a bonus! The ease of plugging in does not effect unplugging, it unplugs just like any other charger and does not fall out.
-The leather strap is personally useless for me since I typically never move my chargers and don't travel, but I still appreciate the accessory. The leather feels durable and the clasp is sturdy. If you are someone who travels frequently or transports your chargers, the strap will make it much more compact and easy.

The negative:
-I hate the visual design. The black with white speckles is supposed to be aesthetically pleasing, but instead it makes the charger look dirty.

All in all, I would say this is a fantastic charger with a great price point. This charger would last much longer than others at similar price points. I will continue to be using this product consistently.

text_fidelity_a:
Sonpre Samurai Max-C Pop-up SD Rechargeable Speaker for Smartphones/Laptops/Tablets/MP3s - Black This is a more upscale version of the “pop up” speakers that have been around for a while. It adds some useful features including an SD card slot to play mp3 files directly and more advanced controls, such as a toggle switch for track skip and a mute button.

When compressed it’s very compact, measuring roughly 2.5 inches in diameter. While it can be played in its compact mode, the sound quality is not all that great – very tinny with little bass.

The sound quality improves significantly when it’s popped open. That increases the height to about 3.25 inches. That doesn't seem like much, but it makes a huge difference in sound quality. The bass is far more pronounced and, while the mid and upper ranges are still somewhat muddy, it’s far more pleasant to listen to than when it is folded up.

Given the size, I’d rate the sound quality as very good when it is in its pop-up mode. This is not a room-filling speaker but it sounds a whole lot better than the internal speakers in a tablet.

It is a direct-connect only speaker – it does NOT have bluetooth. It comes with a 3.5mm cord that is permanently attached to the base of the speaker. The cable can be stowed in a grove on the base of the speaker. The attached cable is a plus and a minus: you’ll never forget to bring a cable along, but the cord is only about 5 inches long, which made it backward to use on some of my equipment. I like that the cord is attached, but it really needs to be a bit longer.

The build quality feels pretty solid. It’s all plastic, as expected, but it has a nice feel to it. The bellows section in the middle feels like it is build solid enough to last a while. Plus, the fact that you can close it up easily for transport gives me some measure of assurance that it will survive being tossed around a bit. For the price, I’d rate the build quality as very good.

There are less expensive pop-up speakers available, such as the Xboom. I have one of those as well, and when comparing the two side-by-side I thought the sound quality was bit better on the Sonpre. The Sonpre also has more features than the Xboom (the mute button in particular is a welcome addition) and has longer battery life. So, while it is a few bucks more, it does bring some additional features to the table.

Although the short cord drops my rating by a star, this is definitely one to consider if you’re looking for a decent sounding pop-up speaker.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Sonpre Samurai Max-C Pop-up SD Rechargeable Speaker for Smartphones/Laptops/Tablets/MP3s - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) I'm not going to delve into the technical aspects of the Fire as others have done an admirable job already. But as an alternative to other, more expensive tablets, the Fire is an amazing piece of tech.

I was almost getting ready to pull the trigger on the Google Pixel C or Samsung S3. A big leap for me as I didn't want to spend $500 plus on a tablet, but I wanted fast speed, large screen, and inexpensive aftermarket accessories.

The Fire is dual-core, so it flies through the games I play. A big plus. I know everyone hates when their game bogs down in the middle of a rousing Orc battle, or, even worse, won't even load. The Fire has run all the games I've thrown at it with no issues.

The 10" screen is heavenly, considering I came from a generic 7" tablet that was VGA on a good day. The text is crisp, the graphics flow as they should. HD movies and shows are freakin' excellent. The 10" format seems to be the best for this.

If you research well for accessories, you can find some nice deals. There was no way I was going to spring for a $30 case, when the $10 Fintie case works as good or better. More money saved for movies, games, and books!

Please don't spend the extra $15 on the 'without special offers' option. The only special offers thrown at you are when the tablet wakes from sleep. A quick swipe and they're gone. Save that money for a case!

And yes, Virginia, you can get the google play store. The easiest way is to install 4 app files and run them in order. No rooting, no PC hookups. Go to blog.ebook-reader dot com and search 'how to install google play on fire.' Easy peasy, just follow the instructions to the letter.

All-in-all this a capable tablet offered by Amazon. The price is right, the tech is excellent considering its price point. You can game like a madman, watch shows, and read War & Peace.

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black Before you buy, check the Monoprice website for this item. The price may be much cheaper over there.

This is a very inexpensive, relatively low quality TV antenna. You get what you pay for. They advertise this for both indoor and outdoor use, but the mostly plastic construction will not last long outdoors in areas that get a lot of wind, ice, or bright sunlight. The attached 3 foot cable really tells you what their intended use case is. If your TV is near a window, hang the antenna in the window, plug it in, and you're done.

The advertised 50 mile range is for ideal conditions, mounting the antenna outdoors in an area where there are absolutely no obstructions between your home and the TV broadcast tower (no trees, no buildings, etc). Expect much worse range for an indoor mounting and if there are any obstructions. If you live in an area with trees etc, you should get a more sturdy antenna that can be mounted on a pole on top of your roof so it can receive a signal over the trees.

This antenna is advertised for UHF frequencies only. Most TV stations use UHF these days, but in my area there are a couple that use VHF and this antenna is not usable for those channels. If you really want VHF, I suggest getting a different antenna from this one.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black

Belkin UltraHD Premium HDMI Cable (2 Meters / 6.6 Feet) This is a very nice, basic cable.

I am surprised that the description does not mention Ethernet support. That concerned me, as it just looks neater having one cable in place of two. However, the cable is printed that it does support Ethernet, and testing it, this is the case. I plugged one end into a receiver that has an Internet connection, the other end into a Raspberry Pi that has no WiFi dongle and it was able to download a file from my DropBox account. I suppose that's such a standard feature, it's not worth mentioning anymore.

The cable seems sturdy enough, but I almost never put my cables through hard use. I set them up and leave them alone. The ends are stiff against bending, which means added support for the most fragile connection. It's reasonably thick, doesn't seem prone to tangling, and does exactly what it should. I am pleased with it.

text_fidelity_a: Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White) I bought tablet  a few days after release. It has super hardware specs and a beautiful screen; however, it seemed to me Samsung rushed its release in order to beat several other tablet coming to market. This Spen is great, yet the Note program needs to be refined to include a few more enhancement similar to the IOS program Notability. There are several bugs that Samsung should have addressed prior to release, and I am sure they will fix with future updates. The bezel appears to be cheap plastic, but I did like the leather back cover. The Polaris Office program is very good but lacks documentation. I returned both of the Notes I tried. One came slightly damaged and both had several software related issues. This does not mean this is a bad product but it is far from polished. I love Samsung and have owned several of their products including a two Samsung Galaxy phones and a Samsung Galaxy 5.0 Player. Their are several positives here, but as it stands now,  this is not a iPad replacement. It is not nearly polished enough and its battery life is not nearly as strong. For $600.00, it should be a lot more refined. I buy the best product from whoever makes it, and I have zero allegiance to any brand. My agenda is about work and productivity, and this product gets it done with several fixable bumps in the road.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White)
